66512.t: ORTHOLOGIC CONJUGATE OF X_4 WRT ABC AND EXCENTRAL
66512.en: In the following, ℓ(⊥AB, P, θ) denotes the line obtained by rotating ℓ(⊥AB, P) by angle θ about P, where ℓ(⊥AB, P) denotes the line through a point P perpendicular to a line AB, and -π/2 < θ ≤ π/2 (counter-clockwise is the positive direction).
re: X_66512 = polar conjugate of the isotomic conjugate of X_17496
X_66512 = cevapoint of X_650 and X_21645.
X_66512 = crossdifference of every pair of points on line {71, 216}
no: Let :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` be two triangles. If there exists θ = θ _0 such that the three lines ℓ(⊥ B_{2}C_{2}, A_{1}, θ _0), ℓ(⊥ C_{2}A_{2}, B_{1}, θ _0), ℓ(⊥ A_{2}B_{2}, C_{1}, θ _0) concur in a point P_{1}, then, the three lines ℓ(⊥ B_{1}C_{1}, A_{2}, -θ _0), ℓ(⊥ C_{1}A_{1}, B_{2}, -θ _0), ℓ(⊥ A_{1}B_{1}, C_{2}, -θ _0) also concur in a point P_{2}. Here, we call :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` the θ _0-isologic triangles . We call P_{1} the isologic center of :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` with respect to A_{2} B_{2} C_{2} , and P_{2} the isologic center of :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` with respect to A_{1} B_{1} C_{1} , and θ _0 the isologic angle of :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and A_{2} B_{2} C_{2} .

Let P be a point in the plane. Let A' = B_{1}C_{1} ∩ ℓ(⊥ PA_{2}, P_{1}, θ _0). Define B', C' cyclically. Similarly, let A'' = B_{2}C_{2} ∩ ℓ(⊥ PA_{1}, P_{2}, -θ _0). Define B'', C'' cyclically. Then, The triangle bounded by A'A'', B'B'', C'C'' is perspective with both :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>`. A', B', C' lie on the same line ℓ_{1}. Similarly, A'', B'', C'' lie on the same line ℓ_{2}. We call ℓ_{1} the :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>`-isologic transversal of P with respect to A_{2} B_{2} C_{2} , and ℓ_{2} the :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>`-isologic transversal of P with respect to A_{1} B_{1} C_{1} . Let Q = ℓ_{1} ∩ ℓ_{2}. Suppose that P_{1} ≢ P_{2}. Let ℓ_{X} be the perpendicular bisector of P_{1}P_{2}. We call ℓ_{X} the isologic axis of :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and A_{2} B_{2} C_{2} . The line PQ passes through a fixed point U on ℓ_{X}, and angle ∡ :g:`P_{2}UP_{1} << P_2 U P_1 >>` = 2*θ _0. We call U the isologic pole of :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and A_{2} B_{2} C_{2} . The mapping f : P → Q is an involution, i.e., f(f(P)) = P. We call Q the isologic conjugate of P with respect to :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and A_{2} B_{2} C_{2} . If P coincides with U, then, ℓ_{1} coincides with ℓ_{2}, and therefore Q is undefined. Let ℓ_{U} be the :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>`-isologic transversal of U with respect to :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` (or equivalently, :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>`-isologic transversal of U with respect to :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>`). We call ℓ_{U} the isologic polar of :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and A_{2} B_{2} C_{2} . Conversely, if P lies on the isologic polar, then Q coincides with the isologic pole U. ℓ_{U} is perpendicular to ℓ_{X}. The intersection point of :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>`-isologic transversal of P and :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>`-isologic transversal of Q lies on ℓ_{U}. Suppose that θ _0 ≠ 0, and P_{1} ≢ P_{2}. Let the circle (:g:`P_{1}P_{2}U << P_1 P_2 U >>`) intersect ℓ_{X} in T different from U. Let T_{1} and T_{2} be the real intersection points of ℓ_{U} and (:g:`P_{1}P_{2}U << P_1 P_2 U >>`). If P lies on the circle centered at T and whose radical axis with (:g:`P_{1}P_{2}U << P_1 P_2 U >>`) is ℓ_{U}, then, Q coincides with P (except for T_{1} and T_{2}), and the triangle bounded by A'A'', B'B'', C'C'' degenerates to a point. Q is also undefined if P coincides with T_{1} or T_{2}.

Note that isologic centers are not necessarily uniquely determined. For example, let ABC be a triangle, and let :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` be the pedal triangles of X_15, X_16, respectively. Then, :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` have infinitely many isologic centers. This is because :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` are inversely similar. Also, if θ _0 = 0 and P_{1} coincides with P_{2}, then, the two isologic transversals of P always coincide, and the isologic conjugate of P is undefined. If θ _0 = 0, then, :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` are orthologic. In this case, we call Q the orthologic conjugate of P with respect to :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and A_{2} B_{2} C_{2} . For example, X_47805 is the orthologic conjugate of X_2 with respect to ABC and the excentral triangle. The orthologic conjugates of X_4, X_6, X_9 with respect to ABC and the excentral triangle were found by Peter Moses, Dec 14, 2024. The line P_{1}P_{2} is the isologic polar. If θ _0 = π/2, then, :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` are parallelogic.
Based on notes by Keita Miyamoto, Dec 3, 2024, updated on Dec 23, 2024.

66553.en: Two triangles related to the original Morley triangles are recovered and renamed here: The **Morley-homothetic-inscribed triangle** is the triangle inscribed in ABC and homothetic to the 1st-, 2nd- and 3rd- Morley triangles. This triangle was introduced by Peter Moses as triangle J_{1} J_{2} J_{3} just before X_3272. Its center is precisely X_3272 and it has A-vertex with trilinear coordinates: J_{1} = 0 : sin((A - C + π)/3) : sin((A - B + π)/3) (See Peter Moses, X_3272) The **Morley-homothetic-circumscribed triangle** is the triangle circumscribed to ABC and homothetic to the 1st-, 2nd- and 3rd- Morley triangles. This triangle is cited by Randy Hutson in a property of X_8011. Its center is X_8011 and it has A-vertex with trilinear coordinates: A" = -1 : (a*(-1+4*z^2)-(2*(y-2*x*z))*c)/((-1+4*z^2)*b-(2*(x-2*y*z))*c): (a*(-1+4*y^2)-(2*(z-2*x*y))*b)/((-1+4*y^2)*c-(2*(x-2*y*z))*b)
no: See Tran Quang Hung and Ercole Suppa, `euclid 7485 <https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/7485>`__.
This preamble and centers X_66554-X_66580 were contributed by César Eliud Lozada, December 23, 2024.

where x = cos(A/3), y = cos(B/3), z = cos(C/3) or, equivalently, A" = cos((2*(B-C))/3)+2*cos((B-C)/3)*sin(A+π/6) : * -2*csc((B-C+π)/3)*sin((A-C+π)/3)*(sin(C)*sin((B-A+π)/3)+sin(A)*sin((B-C+π)/3)) : * -2*csc((C-B+π)/3)*sin((A-B+π)/3)*(sin(B)*sin((C-A+π)/3)+sin(A)*sin((C-B+π)/3))
